newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin cuts electricity prices, sets gas market.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin cuts electricity prices, sets gas market.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin has signed a decree regulating wholesale electricity and rail prices and creating a wholesale natural gas market, the presidential press service said on Monday.
The decree, signed at the weekend, calls for a wholesale gas market to be created on January 1997, but freezes gas prices at their October 1 level until that time.

Gas prices would be set according to the distance that the gas travels from its place of production to users. The wholesale gas market will cover gas provided by Gazprom to distributors, except for gas intended for residential consumers.

The decree, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, also cuts wholesale electricity charges for both industrial and residential customers by an average 10 percent starting November 1 from their August 1 levels.
Growth in wholesale and residential electricity prices in the first half of 1997 should not exceed growth in the wholesale producer price index, the document said.
In the first eight months of this year the overall index of producer prices rose 18.3 percent, while the index of electrical energy prices rose 27.3 percent, State Statistics Committee figures show.
The decree recommends regional energy commissions to set electricity and thermal energy prices for all categories of users at a level based on the actual cost of production and distribution.
Charges for transport by rail using electric locomotives will also be governed by the new electricity pricing rules from November 1.
It said the government would take additional measures to limit rises in rail transport charges and establish a new procedure by April 1997 for setting and regulating such prices.

Under the decree, natural gas monopoly RAO Gazprom GAZP.RTS #0.GAZP.RUO will be liable for excise and profits tax on proceeds from collecting debts for the supply of gas, as long as these proceeds are not lower than Gazprom's actual cost of producing and transmitting the gas.
